name: RAKBANK (The National Bank of Ras Al Khaimah)
legal_name: The National Bank of Ras Al-Khaimah (P.S.C.)

ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. The Government of Ras Al Khaimah owns 49.35% and Mr Ahmed Essa Al Naeem 6.96% (31 Dec 2025, integrated report; same figures on the IR page as of 31 Jul 2025). The H1 2026 financial statements state the Bank is controlled by the Government of Ras Al Khaimah by majority of voting rights.

shareholders.holder: Mr Ahmed Essa Ahmed Al Naeem

government_link: Yes — Government of Ras Al Khaimah holds 49.35% and controls the Bank by majority of voting rights (31 Dec 2025 / 30 Jun 2026).
group_structure: Parent bank with an Islamic banking window (RAKislamic). Subsidiaries at 30 Jun 2026: Ras Al Khaimah National Insurance Company PSC (RAKInsurance, 79.23%), BOSS FZCO (back office, 80% legal / 100% beneficial), RAK Technologies FZCO (under liquidation), Protego Insurance Brokers L.L.C. (100%), RAKAZA (Management Office) (100%), plus RAKBANK Digital Assets LLC (incorporated 2025 to issue payment tokens; capital infusion in progress). No asset-management or brokerage subsidiary; brokerage runs inside the bank under its own capital-markets licence.

RAKAZA (Management Office)

footprint: UAE only: 19 branches and two electronic banking units (30 Jun 2026); branches in Ras Al Khaimah, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman and Fujairah; Elite centres in Dubai (Opus Tower), Abu Dhabi (Omnia Tower) and Ras Al Khaimah.
customer_segments: Personal Banking (mass market, Select, Elite affluent tier, non-resident Elite, microsegment of blue-collar workers), Business Banking (SME — core franchise), Wholesale Banking (corporates, financial institutions), Islamic banking (RAKislamic).
business_lines: Personal Banking (cards, loans, mortgages, deposits, Elite/Select premium banking and wealth: funds, bonds and fractional bonds, sukuk, structured products, wealth lending, digital gold/silver, in-app global equities and crypto); Business Banking (SME); Wholesale Banking (corporate, FI, treasury, DCM, trade); RAKislamic window; insurance (RAKInsurance, Protego); Skiply education/family payments app. Merchant acquiring sold to Network International in Mar 2026.

capabilities.wealth_summary: RAKBANK runs wealth inside Personal Banking through a two-tier premium model, Select and Elite (Euromoney's Middle East and UAE 'best for premier banking' 2026). Elite gives a dedicated relationship manager, Elite centres in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah, and remote onboarding for non-residents. The shelf is third-party: mutual funds (Franklin Templeton, Legg Mason, BlackRock Aditum), bonds, fractional bonds and sukuk, structured products, wealth lending and digital gold/silver. In-app it offers 30,000+ international stocks and ETFs (Rakbank Digital Equities, execution-only, conventional only) and 21 cryptocurrencies through Bitpanda (from Jul 2025; Bitcoin for Islamic customers from Aug 2026). The bank says wealth management income rose 34% and AUM 11% in 2025 but discloses no AUM; fiduciary assets were AED 6.8bn at 30 Jun 2026. 2026 priority: 'expand wealth management offerings - broaden the product suite and digitise wealth journeys'.

segments.eligibility: Entry premium tier (Euromoney); published threshold not found

segments.name: Rakbank Elite
segments.eligibility: Not published on the Elite page; dedicated Elite RM, Elite centres, preferential FX, lower equities trading fee (0.15% vs 0.20%)

private_banking.detail: No private-banking unit or proposition is named. Premium clients are served through Select and Elite, which Euromoney describes as aimed at affluent professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging HNW clients 'often underserved by traditional private banking models'.

asset_management.detail: No asset-management subsidiary among the Group's subsidiaries; funds offered are third-party ('RAKBANK is not the issuer of the Product').

brokerage.detail: Rakbank Digital Equities: execution-only trading of global stocks and ETFs (incl. fractional shares) in the mobile app; US fee 0.15% (Elite) or 0.20% (Select/Personal), min USD 1; Europe/UK from 0.22%. The bank states it is licensed by the UAE Capital Market Authority to provide execution-only trading (licence 20200000373). Execution and custody via unnamed 'Third Party Providers'. Zero-fee promotion to 31 Oct 2026. Conventional only - no Islamic variant.

digital_investing.detail: Rakbank mobile app: 30,000+ international stocks and ETFs, digital gold and silver from 1 gram, 21 cryptocurrencies (via Bitpanda, launched Jul 2025, invitation-only at launch), digital mutual fund subscription journey (2025). A new Personal Banking app was launched in 2026.

advisory.detail: Relationship-manager-led advice for Elite clients ('expert guidance, tailored solutions'), with access to global fixed income, international fund managers, FX trading, structured products and lending. A 2025 sponsored feature lists mutual funds, bonds, structured products, insurance, digital gold, FX trading and margin lending.

discretionary.detail: No discretionary mandate or managed-portfolio service found on wealth pages or in the integrated report.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advice or model portfolio offering found.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party funds incl. Franklin Templeton Investment Funds, Legg Mason Global Funds and BlackRock Aditum Global Allocation / Multi-Asset Income funds; conventional and Shariah-compliant funds. Platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: Capital-protected, partially protected and non-guaranteed structured products listed on the investment products page.

private_markets.detail: No private-markets or alternatives product found on wealth pages or in reports.

islamic_wealth.detail: RAKislamic window: Shariah-compliant mutual funds and sukuk on the shelf; Bitcoin trading for RAKislamic customers via Bitpanda from Aug 2026. Equities brokerage and wealth lending are conventional only.

opportunities: Stated 2026 priority to broaden the wealth product suite and digitise wealth journeys (S4 p.28).
Shelf has no discretionary mandates, model portfolios or private-markets products; funds come from a few houses (Franklin Templeton, Legg Mason, BlackRock) (S11, S12).
Fast-growing affluent franchise: wealth management income +34% and AUM +11% in 2025; Euromoney 2026 premier-banking awards for Select/Elite (S4, S20).
Islamic customers have limited investing options: equities brokerage and wealth lending are conventional only (S14, S11).
barriers: Already built in-app investing itself in 2025–2026 (global equities via unnamed third-party providers, crypto via Bitpanda, digital gold) (S13, S17).
Heavy in-house technology build: microservices platform on AWS, Databricks, Microsoft; Finacle core (S4).
Focus is SME and mass/affluent retail rather than HNW private banking; no published Elite threshold or AUM figure (S16, S20).
incumbent_vendors: AWS, Databricks, Microsoft — cloud, data and AI (S4)
Franklin Templeton, Legg Mason, BlackRock — third-party funds (S12)

Lead check — Infosys Finacle: supported. The 2025 integrated report plans migration of Islamic banking core systems to Finacle in 2026 and cites Finacle awards; the 2013 Infosys implementation release was seen in search results only (403). Finacle is core banking, not a wealth platform.
Lead check — RAKBANK stakes in fintechs: no equity stake in any fintech found. Partnerships found instead: Bitpanda, Network International, AWS, Databricks, Microsoft.
Equities execution broker/custodian not named in the KFS or T&Cs ('Third Party Providers'). Launch date of Rakbank Digital Equities not published.

No named head of wealth or Elite on the official management page or in the 2025 integrated report; Elite and Select eligibility thresholds are not published. A role-based LinkedIn search on 2026-10-13 returned a profile 'Nabeel Batlay - RAKBANK' whose search summary gave the title 'Head of Wealth Management and Customer Segments'; the title and a Forbes Middle East panel mention could not be confirmed (LinkedIn cannot be opened, panel page not found). He is not on the official page, so he was not added; verify through RAKBANK or a dated source before use.

Executive-moves listing (Fundz, dated 12 Sep 2026) reports Tapas Kumar Mondal as Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer - Digital and AI (digital channels, technology, engineering and AI); a search summary of a LinkedIn post puts that announcement about 626 days before 13 Oct 2026 (early 2025), so the date is unresolved. He is not on the official page and no RAKBANK release was found; not added. Michael Power (Group COO in the 2025 integrated report) is no longer listed; no departure news found.

Not profiled (outside the pass scope of decision-makers, board members already in the file and the heads of retail/wealth/digital/technology): six directors with bios on the board page (Salem Ali Al Sharhan, Jonathan Edward Morris, Abhijit Choudhury, Debra Ward, Mohammed Abdulrahman Aljallaf, Sheikh Abdulla Khalid Al Qassimi; first elected 2012, 2023, 2024, 2024, 2024, 2024 per the 2025 integrated report); Group Chief HR Officer, General Counsel, Chief Audit Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Credit Officer and Group Chief Compliance Officer (S9); Chief of Staff and the RAKInsurance Chief Executive Officer (S4 PDF p.63).

LinkedIn (2026-10-13): one search-result match recorded (DJ Choi, S29). Role-based searches for the Group CEO, personal banking, wealth, technology and chairman returned no matching profile, so those stay 'Not verified'.
